intro.heading: Take time over the movements you are learning
paragraphs: Starting exercise after a setback can bring plenty of questions. You may want to try a movement slowly, ask about resistance or work out what feels manageable on that day. A one-to-one session gives you time for that conversation.
Alpha offers individual reformer Clinical Pilates at our Newport clinic. The session is centred on your exercises, with guidance from a clinician and adjustments based on your needs.
Tell us what you would like to work towards and anything that has been difficult. Suitability needs to be considered before choosing exercises.

intro.caption: One-to-one reformer Clinical Pilates is offered in Newport.

explainer.heading: What is Clinical Pilates?
paragraphs: Pilates is a form of exercise that can use a mat or equipment. A reformer has a moving carriage and spring resistance, which can be adjusted for different exercises. You do not need to know the equipment before asking about a session.

Alpha offers one-to-one reformer sessions. Your health history and goals inform the exercises you practise. This individual appointment format gives you room to discuss symptoms, ask questions and change the pace.
The Victorian Better Health Channel Pilates guide explains the different formats and the value of advice when you have a health condition, are pregnant or have recently had surgery.

benefits.heading: Guidance as you practise
benefits.intro: Tell the clinician how each exercise feels. That feedback helps them adjust the session.

items.title: A pace you can discuss
items.copy: Take time to learn an exercise and tell the clinician how it feels. Repetitions and rest can be considered as part of the session.

items.title: Adjustable resistance
items.copy: Reformer springs offer different resistance options. The clinician considers which setting and movement are suitable for you.

items.title: Feedback as you practise
items.copy: Ask about the exercise and discuss any discomfort. Guidance can help you understand what you are being asked to do.

items.title: Review your exercises
items.copy: The exercises can be revisited as your circumstances change. Your response and goals guide any changes.

conditions.heading: Talk about your circumstances first
conditions.intro: A condition name alone does not decide whether Pilates is suitable. Let the clinician know about symptoms, medical advice and any restrictions.

items.title: Back pain
items.copy: Discuss the movements that bother you and any assessment or advice you have received. Exercises may need changing before you try them.

items.title: Pregnancy-related pain
items.copy: Your maternity team remains responsible for pregnancy care. Ask about exercise suitability and tell us about any advice or restrictions they have given you.

items.title: Hypermobility
items.copy: Bring up joint symptoms and activities that have been difficult. Exercise choice and range need individual consideration.

visit.heading: Getting started with Clinical Pilates
visit.intro: Ask about an individual Pilates appointment through our booking flow or reception. We can help you check the available practitioner.

steps.title: Explain your goals
steps.copy: Talk about your exercise experience, health history and what you would like to practise. Include recent surgery or changes in symptoms.

steps.title: Consider suitability
steps.copy: The clinician considers what is appropriate for you and whether further advice or assessment is needed before proceeding.

steps.title: Practise with guidance
steps.copy: Work through selected exercises and discuss how they feel. The pace or resistance can be adjusted during the session.

steps.title: Discuss the next step
steps.copy: Review the session and talk about ongoing exercise. Further appointments depend on your goals and response.

notes.title: What to wear
notes.copy: Choose comfortable clothing you can move in. Ask reception if you are unsure about any preparation or equipment requirements.

notes.title: Medical advice matters
notes.copy: Tell us about any restrictions from your treating team. Pregnancy or recent surgery calls for an individual suitability discussion.

team.heading: Guidance from Pilates-trained clinicians
team.copy: Lara Trevorrow is an osteopath with a clinic-listed Certificate IV in Pilates and experience in one-to-one Pilates rehabilitation. Other Pilates-trained clinicians also work at Alpha. Check the current appointment options when booking; the available practitioner may vary.

faqs.question: Do I need Pilates experience?
faqs.answer: You can ask about a session without having used a reformer before. Tell the clinician about your exercise experience so the guidance can start at an appropriate level.

faqs.question: Are these group classes?
faqs.answer: Alpha offers one-to-one reformer Clinical Pilates sessions in Newport. Ask reception about the current appointment options.

faqs.question: How does it compare with a studio class?
faqs.answer: Alpha offers an individual appointment informed by your health history and goals. Studio formats vary, so check what is included with the provider you are considering.

faqs.question: Can I do Clinical Pilates while pregnant?
faqs.answer: Discuss exercise with your maternity team and tell the clinician about your pregnancy and any restrictions. Suitability and exercise choice need individual assessment; Pilates is not automatically appropriate for every pregnancy.

faqs.question: What if I have recently had surgery?
faqs.answer: Follow your treating team’s instructions and let us know about the procedure and any restrictions. The clinician may need further information before deciding which exercises are appropriate.

faqs.question: Do I need a referral?
faqs.answer: You can enquire about a private appointment without a referral. Bring relevant advice from your treating team. Funding arrangements can have separate requirements.

faqs.question: Can I use private health insurance?
faqs.answer: Eligibility depends on your cover, the service and the practitioner providing it. Ask reception and your insurer before attending. A Pilates appointment does not automatically attract a rebate.

faqs.question: How many sessions will I need?
faqs.answer: That depends on your goals and how you respond. Discuss a review point with the clinician rather than assuming a fixed number of sessions.

closing.heading: Find an appointment that fits
closing.copy: Look for a one-to-one Pilates appointment in online booking, or call 03 9962 5539 to discuss suitability and the available practitioner.
